newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia unveils ambitious privatization plan.
newsitem.headline: Colombia unveils ambitious privatization plan.

text.p: Colombia plans to raise at least $1.28 billion by mid-December through an ambitious privatization program featuring the sale of four electrical power plants and a minority stake in one of the world's largest nickel producers, government officials said Tuesday.

Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo and Energy and Mines Minister Rodrigo Villamizar announced the privatizations after a cabinet meeting. During the session, the plan to sell off assets valued at a minimum of 1.34 trillion pesos ($1.28 bln) was finalized, they said.

The centerpiece is the sale of the four electric power plants, including the huge Chivor hydroelectric facility in central Boyaca province and the Betania hydroelectric plant in southwestern Huila province.
Villamizar said sale of the plants should raise more than $1 billion. Chivor and Betania alone were valued at $990 million, he said.
The government also expected to raise more than $172 million through the sale of its 47.7 percent stake in Cerro Matoso SA, the world's fourth-largest nickel mine, Ocampo said.
In the past, Ocampo has said that South Africa's Gencor Ltd, which owns a 52.3 percent interest in the mine, was among the prospective buyers of the government stake.
The government will also put on the auction block its 61 percent interest in Concasa, the country's fifth-largest savings and loan. It hopes to raise $105.4 million through that sale, Ocampo said.
He said the goverment expected to complete all the privatizations by mid-December.
